condition.label: femoroacetabular impingement syndrome
condition.distinctions: Symptoms/signs plus morphology define syndrome; incidental morphology alone is not this condition. Separate OA and postoperative protocols.

scope.stage: Nonoperative; source populations largely surgical candidates or cam morphology.
scope.operativeStatus: Nonoperative rehabilitation only; postoperative pathways require separate assessment.
scope.exclusions: Established OA, prior surgery, dysplasia/other pathology need separate review.
scope.uncertainty: Source eligibility limits applicability; it does not establish contraindications.

sources.title: Hip arthroscopy versus best conservative care for the treatment of femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (UK FASHIoN): a multicentre randomised controlled trial
sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication, before access date.

access.details: Primary full text inspected at linked archive/publisher; Europe PMC XML used where PMC HTML challenged.

integrity.method: Primary metadata and retrieved text inspected; regional update searches. Bounded check, not registry-wide clearance.
integrity.result: No notice identified in inspected text; no formal replacement established.

sources.population: Age≥ 16, symptomatic cam/pincer morphology, considered surgical candidates; no established OA or prior shape-changing surgery.
sources.coInterventions: Education, pain relief; optional injection in conservative arm.
sources.outcomes: 12-month iHOT-33 adjusted difference 6.8 (1.7–12.0) favored surgery; both groups improved.
sources.uncertainty: Unblinded, no untreated control; surgical comparison cannot prove exercise harm.
sources.harms: Muscle soreness common; adverse events self-reported 6 weeks; serious events hospital-reported.
sources.limitations: Not clinical approval or a universal ordinary-training restriction.

sources.title: Physiotherapist-led treatment for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (the PhysioFIRST study): an assessor-blinded, limited disclosure randomised controlled trial
sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication, before access date.

access.details: Primary full text inspected at linked archive/publisher; Europe PMC XML used where PMC HTML challenged.

integrity.method: Primary metadata and retrieved text inspected; regional update searches. Bounded check, not registry-wide clearance.

sources.population: Nonoperative cam-related FAI; prior hip/back surgery and OA excluded.
sources.comparator: Standardized stretching with equal contact/gym access.
sources.outcomes: Six-month iHOT-33 difference 0.2 (−5.9 to 6.3); no primary superiority. Dichotomized pain improvement OR 2.36 (1.15–4.84) favored strength.
sources.uncertainty: No usual-care arm; COVID stopped recruitment; editorial roles disclosed; NHMRC funded.
sources.harms: Two adverse/one serious event, all unrelated; no treatment-related event reported.
sources.limitations: Not clinical approval or a universal ordinary-training restriction.

protocol.execution: Individual hip/trunk strength, functional/plyometric work and activity plan.
protocol.frequency: First 3 months: weekly supervised plus 2 home/week; later gym/home and monthly consults.

findings.statement: 12-month iHOT-33 adjusted difference 6.8 (1.7–12.0) favored surgery; both groups improved.
findings.applicability: Age≥ 16, symptomatic cam/pincer morphology, considered surgical candidates; no established OA or prior shape-changing surgery.
findings.limitations: Unblinded, no untreated control; surgical comparison cannot prove exercise harm.

findings.statement: PHT advises reducing impingement-provoking daily positions and excludes painful hard-end stretching.

proposedRules.statement: Consider modifying symptom-provoking impingement positions and painful end-range stretching during review; no numeric ROM cap.

gaps: All material is draft and clinically unreviewed; no runtime mapping, supported-condition claim, default dose or escalation clearance follows.
No universal numeric load/range cap or hard exercise contraindication was established; benefit from alternatives and trial exclusions do not prove harm.
Concurrent condition restrictions, equipment requirements and independent joint limits remain controlling; stretching never earns strength-set credit or generic five-second progression.
No single exact exercise execution shared by individualized packages was verified; no exercise request invented from muscle-group names.
Movement advice is published consensus within care packages, not proof every deep squat, hip rotation or stretch is harmful.
Long-term structural protection and precise individualized safe ROM remain unresolved.
